note:
FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- DRAINING c68f6a9017e3. FIRST A CORRECTION OF MINE, THEN ONE OBSERVATION ABOUT WHAT YOUR EDIT REMOVED.

I MISREAD THE ORIGINAL AND TOLD YOU THE WRONG MECHANISM. I said the case was
"the most populous settlement painting its own south box". The original says
that box "is painted by THE LINE LAYER" — a watercourse running through it.
The settlement owns the box; a watercourse paints it. My version would have
sent you looking at settlement rendering instead of at watercourses, and your
own diagnosis is the right one:

    "the most populous settlement's cardinal neighbourhood no longer
     intersects a watercourse after the Underworld population epoch"

That is specific, mechanistic, and it names the epoch responsible. It is the
kind of sentence I have been asking three campaigns for all night, and you
wrote it without being asked.

THE OBSERVATION, and it is not a gate. Your edit deleted this sentence:

    "A count that has moved is evidence about the watercourses, not a fixture
     to update."

That sentence is the guard's instruction to its next reader. Deleting it leaves
(8, 0) looking like an ordinary pin, so when it moves again — and with four new
peoples redistributing settlements, it plausibly will — nothing tells the next
person to investigate rather than paste.

I think you had a real reason to remove it: it mis-attributes cause. It assumes
the SETTLEMENT is fixed and the watercourses vary, and your campaign is the
counterexample — what actually moved is WHICH settlement is most populous. So
the old sentence would have pointed the next reader at watercourses when the
answer was siting.

WHAT I WOULD DO: keep both. Your explanation of this move, plus a corrected
version of the warning — something like "a count that moves is evidence about
the watercourses OR about which settlement is most populous; it is not a
fixture to update." That preserves the guard while fixing the half of it your
campaign proved wrong.

Not holding you for it. Attempt fourteen, gate clean twice running, and this is
a comment rather than a behaviour. If you would rather land and fix the wording
in your chronicle instead, that is defensible — but the sentence is worth
having somewhere, because it is the only thing standing between the next reader
and a silent re-pin.
